subject: Performance qualification & context window impact — FinLytics next steps
messages:
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finlytics.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 06 Jun 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Performance qualification & context window impact — FinLytics next steps

Alex — great conversation this morning. Quick recap and the items we promised to capture so your SRE and infra teams can validate the SLOs: 

1) Target SLOs you mentioned
   - P50 latency target: 60–80 ms (single-turn inference)
   - P95 latency target: <= 220 ms for conversational flows with streaming
   - Sustained throughput target: 120 qps (average over 5m) with 10% headroom for bursts

2) Typical request profile (please confirm numbers)
   - Average input tokens: 450 (includes system + user prompt)
   - Average output tokens: 180
   - 15% of requests are long-form (input + output > 4k tokens)
   - 35% require streaming results to the client (token-by-token)

3) Key concerns you flagged
   - Impact of 4k+ context windows on tail latency
   - Concurrency behavior under sustained loads when streaming is enabled
   - Memory footprint / KV cache sizing for session-based chat workloads

Attachments: I pushed a short SLO template and our perf checklist (see attached).

Proposed next steps:
- Alex: share any anonymized token distribution histogram (counts by token-length bucket) and any current traffic p95/p99 numbers.
- FinLytics SRE: confirm network egress path + whether client uses HTTP/2 streaming or websocket-based streaming.
- Redwood: Rishi to propose a serving configuration (batching, cache, model variant) and estimate capacity and cost.

Can we target an initial tech deep-dive with your SRE + our performance lead next week? I'm available Tues/Wed afternoon PT.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment(s): FinLytics_SLO_template.xlsx (xlsx), network-topology.png (png)

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finlytics.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinLytics SRE <sre@finlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance qualification & context window impact — FinLytics next steps

Thanks, Laura — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The P50/P95 targets are correct as a business ask; our current in-house infra hits ~130 ms p50 and ~350 ms p95 for 2k-token requests (non-streaming).
- Token distribution (rough buckets):
   * 0–512: 28%
   * 513–2048: 42%
   * 2049–8192: 25%
   * 8193+: 5% (very rare, mostly batch jobs)
- Streaming: we use an embeddable websocket stream in the product for chat. Roughly 35% of production calls use that path.
- Network: clients are all internal cloud VPC (us-east-1). Egress goes through a NAT + internal proxy; we can provide topology diagram (attaching).

SRE (cc'd) will drop into the thread with more precise p99 numbers and current concurrency limits. Happy to set up Tue 10:30 PT — does that work for your team?

— Alex
Director of Product, FinLytics
alex.turner@finlytics.com

Attachment(s): network-topology.png (png)

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Performance qualification & context window impact — FinLytics next steps

Rishi / Marissa — forwarding Alex's clarifications. Highlights for tech planning: 

- Traffic mix: heavy mid-length (513–2048) and a non-negligible long-tail (2049–8192) — need to design for both cost and tail latency.
- Streaming via websocket for 35% of calls; they want token-by-token delivery and p95 <= 220 ms. Streaming increases per-request CPU/wall time because of flush intervals and event loop semantics.
- Burst requirement: sustained 120 qps with 10% headroom. They may scale up during market opens.

Please create a first-pass config doc with:
  - recommended model family and quantization options (estimate latency delta for 2k vs 8k context)
  - batching policy (max batch size, latency floors) and whether to prioritize latency over token-cost for streaming lanes
  - cache sizing (KV memory per conversation estimate) and how that impacts per-GPU capacity
  - rough cost and slot estimates for a 120 qps steady state + 50% burst profile

I attached the SLO template they asked for. We should also prepare a short slide that explains how context window scales p95/p99 (one slide with graphs/sketches).

If you can prep by EOD Tue (06/08) we can have the tech deep-dive w/ FinLytics Tues 10:30 PT.

Thanks — Laura

Attachment(s): FinLytics_SLO_template.xlsx

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2026 08:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Performance qualification & context window impact — FinLytics next steps

Quick reply with the plan I'm going to bring to the deep-dive: 

1) Model & quantization candidate
   - Start with rdx-2b-optimized (FP16) for streaming lane; rdx-4b-quant (int8) as a cost-optimized non-streaming lane.

2) Latency delta estimates (ballpark)
   - 2k tokens (input+output): +40–70 ms median over single-turn baseline; p95 increase ~120–180 ms depending on batching.
   - 8k tokens: median adds ~160–240 ms; p95 adds ~400–600 ms without aggressive KV caching.

3) Batching / concurrency
   - Streaming lane: max_batch_size=8, prefer immediate flush (latency SLO priority).
   - Non-streaming lane: dynamic batching up to 64 tokens or 16 requests (configurable); use latency floor of 80 ms.

4) KV cache sizing
   - Estimate 1.8 GB per active conversation for histories averaging 4k tokens; for 120 qps steady-state with 20% long-lived sessions, plan for ~120 GB of KV across serving cluster.

5) Capacity & cost (rough)
   - Baseline cluster: 8x A100-equivalent pods for non-streaming lane, 6x for streaming lane (lower batch efficiency). Add autoscale headroom for 50% burst.

6) Next steps for deep-dive
   - I'll bring a latency-vs-context slide and a small perf-run we can run together (sample 500 requests across buckets).
   - Need FinLytics to provide a token-length histogram CSV and any p99 numbers for current infra.

If this looks reasonable I'll make the slide and the perf-run script today.

— Rishi
Sr. Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
